name: ninja-forms
notes: DUO-3222/DUO-3223 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract): plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — ninja-forms/ninja-forms.php. The original broad 3.x claim was disproved by the boundary harness on the repository's PHP runtime: official releases 3.0.34.2 and 3.1.10 call PHP's removed create_function(), while 3.2.28 and 3.3.21.4 fatal on an invalid parent call during normal plugin boot. Official 3.4.34.2 is the first available archived release that boots and runs the real bundled Job Application fixture, so the certified range is [3.4.34.2, 4.0.0); widening beyond it is DUO-3224's ratification job, not invented here.

Task #75 CLOSED (was: Grind R1-A's honest-partial marker). This manifest now captures a Ninja Forms form's actual content — nf3_forms/nf3_fields/nf3_actions + their _meta twins — via the typed-snapshot grammar in agent/src/Repository/Snapshot.php. Real schema DESCRIBE'd live on NF 3.14.11 again for THIS implementation (not reused from the R1-A report's summary alone): nf3_forms has 14 columns (id, title, key, created_at, updated_at, views, subs, form_title, default_label_pos, show_title, clear_complete, hide_complete, logged_in, seq_num); nf3_fields.parent_id and nf3_actions.parent_id are PLAIN single-target integer FKs into nf3_forms.id, confirmed via SHOW CREATE TABLE to carry no real FOREIGN KEY constraint at all (ordinary WordPress-plugin practice) — so a phase-1 placeholder of 0 is always safe. nf3_forms.key was empirically NULL on the live Job Application fixture, contradicting task #75's own one-line speculation that it might serve as a natural key — mapped identity is used for all three tables. Because plugin rows cannot carry `_duo_uuid`, durability is supplied by duo_map plus the versioned, database-matched identity recovery sidecar; populated restores without it block rather than minting or rebinding identities (DUO-3209).

DUO-3328 narrows the deletion contract without weakening deletion-guard locking. Ninja Forms 3.14.11 ships nf3_actions.parent_id and nf3_fields.parent_id without complete indexes, so InnoDB cannot take the next-key/gap locks required to close concurrent reverse-reference insertion around nf3_forms deletion. Duo does not own a production schema migration for the unmodified plugin and therefore does not advertise table:nf3_forms deletion. Removing a whole form graph now fails atomically during capture with the exact unsupported selector and publishes no partial child tombstones. Independently removing an nf3_action or nf3_field remains supported because those child selectors require only their declared attached-meta cascades.

A genuinely important empirical finding, not assumed: nf3_form_meta/nf3_field_meta/nf3_action_meta DUPLICATE a large fraction of their owning row's real COLUMNS as mirrored meta KEYS of the same name (e.g. nf3_field_meta carries 'label'/'key'/'type'/'order'/'label_pos'/'required'/'parent_id' — all ALSO real nf3_fields columns, with byte-identical values in every row inspected). This is Ninja Forms' own internal redundancy (its model layer merges column + meta into one flat settings array — Abstracts/Model.php/ModelFactory.php), not a Duo design choice, and this manifest does not try to deduplicate it: both the column and its meta mirror are captured and replayed verbatim, exactly as the plugin itself maintains them. Attempting to omit the redundant meta copy would be a subtractive 'cleanup' this project's byte-fidelity discipline explicitly does not attempt.

The dual key/value + meta_key/meta_value column pair on all three _meta tables (verified via DESCRIBE, not assumed from the R1-A report's phrasing) is confirmed, on every real row inspected, to hold byte-identical content in both pairs — a back-compat artifact Ninja Forms' own write path (Database/Models/*.php) maintains by writing both simultaneously. This manifest reads from meta_key/meta_value (the 'current' pair, key_column/value_column) and WRITES both pairs on apply (legacy_key_column/legacy_value_column: key/value) to match what the plugin's own code does, rather than silently letting the legacy pair go stale.

The nf3_upgrades cache hazard (task #75's #5, reproduced empirically in docs/grind/r1a-forms.md: an id-reused form silently serves the PREVIOUS form's stale cached settings) is fixed via a per-row 'invalidate' declaration on nf3_forms, NOT a wp-cli rebuilder (Ninja Forms ships none — 'wp help nf' fails, confirmed again for this task) and NOT a proactively-rebuilt cache (unnecessary — see below). Traced to Ninja Forms' own source rather than guessed: WPN_Helper::delete_nf_cache($id) (includes/Helper.php) does exactly `DELETE FROM nf3_upgrades WHERE id=$id` + `delete_option('nf_form_'.$id)` (a legacy pre-table cache, confirmed empty of nf_form_* options on this fixture but declared defensively anyway), and its own read site (Abstracts/ModelFactory.php's constructor: `if ($form_cache && isset($form_cache['settings'])) { ... }`) correctly falls through to a FRESH read straight from nf3_forms/nf3_fields the moment the cache is simply ABSENT — confirmed by reading the exact conditional, not by trial and error. So invalidating (not rebuilding) after every apply-time write to a form's own row is sufficient: `"invalidate": [{"table": "nf3_upgrades", "column": "id"}, {"option_pattern": "nf_form_{id}"}]`.

The genuinely good news, unchanged from Grind R1-A and still true: submissions do NOT live in these custom tables. nf_sub posts (ordinary wp_postmeta) already round-trip through Duo's existing post/postmeta machinery; nf3_objects/nf3_object_meta/nf3_relationships were confirmed EMPTY of submission data in that round and stay classified runtime here, defensively. nf3_chunks: no FK-shaped column, no confirmed authored content — runtime.
nf_sub stays classified runtime here as a defensive backstop; the real protection is that site.duo.json's policy.post_types must never list it (visitor-submitted, never site-builder-authored).

The block_attrs entry above closes the OTHER half of task #75's acceptance criteria (a page embedding the form via block must render/submit correctly on the target — confirmed empirically live-wired, not by inspection alone: capturing the Careers fixture page BEFORE this entry existed left `{"formID":1,...}` as a raw, unrewritten local id — task #76's fixed regex correctly flagged it as unregistered_block_attr, exactly as intended). `"kind": "nf3_form"` resolves through the SAME generalized Tokens::id_to_token()/token_to_id() this manifest's table refs already use — Blocks.php never hardcoded which kinds are valid, so no engine change beyond Tokens.php's own generalization was needed for a block attribute to reference a table's id_kind. A real ordering hazard surfaced wiring this live, worth recording: Capture::build() runs table capture (which mints nf3_form identity into duo_map) BEFORE building any post body — capturing tables only AFTER post bodies would leave formID silently unrewritten even with this rule declared, since Tokens::id_to_token() would find no ledger entry yet.

`nf3_actions.active` and `nf3_fields.order` are declared `lint_ok: true` deliberately, not to silence noise blindly: both are small integers that coincide with real post/term ids on any small test fixture (order=1..23 walks straight through this site's own post ids 1-16; active=1 matches term id 1, 'Uncategorized') — reviewed and confirmed genuinely NOT refs (active is a boolean 0/1 flag; order is the field/action's own display position within its form, both plain WooCommerce.json-style audited exemptions, the same escape hatch as woocommerce.json's `queryId`).

Every BIT(1) boolean column (nf3_forms.show_title/clear_complete/hide_complete/logged_in, nf3_fields.required/personally_identifiable) is ALSO declared `lint_ok: true`, proactively rather than reactively: their only two possible values are 0/1, which WILL eventually coincide with some real entity's small id on some fixture (confirmed live: this manifest's own conformance-scale test site tripped show_title/clear_complete/hide_complete against term id 1 the first time this was wired end-to-end) — marking the whole COLUMN, not chasing whichever specific collision today's data happens to produce, is the correct, stable exemption for a column whose value space structurally excludes ever holding a ref.

Task #76 (Lint's looks_like_id_attr()/looks_like_id_key() missing the all-caps 'ID' suffix, e.g. Ninja Forms' own Gutenberg block attribute 'formID') is CLOSED separately (agent/src/Review/Lint.php) — this manifest declares no block_attrs entry of its own because 'formID' now matches the fixed heuristic directly; nothing manifest-level was ever needed for that specific finding once the regex was widened.

DUO-3267 follow-up: the nf3_upgrades cache note above (task #75's #5) covers the read-side safety of an ABSENT cache row (ModelFactory's constructor falls through to a fresh nf3_forms/nf3_fields read) but was verified against the id-REUSE scenario specifically, never against a fresh target's OWN first-ever render of a form it just received via apply. Grind R1-A's round-trip leg exercised that exact case for the first time (a genuinely new nf3_forms/nf3_fields/nf3_actions row set, fetched over real HTTP immediately after apply) and found the Careers page's Job Application form render EMPTY on the first fetch, correct on every fetch after -- reproduced twice, identical signature both times, confirmed NOT a curl-truncation or byte-count artifact (both fetches passed a byte-count floor; only the content differed). Traced further than the existing note does: `ModelFactory::get_fields()` (Abstracts/ModelFactory.php, a SEPARATE read site from the constructor's own settings-only check already documented above) ALSO consults `WPN_Helper::get_nf_cache()` -- gated by `WPN_Helper::use_cache()`, which unconditionally `return`s `true` as its very first line, so this check runs for every form, every request, no version gate. Confirmed the existing `invalidate` declaration on nf3_forms DOES fire correctly for a freshly-inserted row, not just a pre-existing one -- Snapshot.php's `finalize_row()` (phase 2) runs `run_invalidate()` unconditionally for every row it finalizes, whether that row was just created by `ensure_row()`'s phase-1 insert or already existed; `run_invalidate()` itself is a plain, correctly-guarded `DELETE FROM nf3_upgrades WHERE id=$localId`. So the documented safety net DOES engage here, on paper -- which is exactly what made this genuinely hard to pin down further by reading alone (as opposed to task #75's own cleanly-reproduced id-reuse case). Not fully resolved: WHY a stale or premature nf3_upgrades row still exists at the moment of the first fetch despite invalidate firing correctly is not confirmed with live evidence (blocked on sandbox pair budget at investigation time, not attempted and abandoned) -- a live-firing candidate worth checking first, not yet checked: whether Ninja Forms' OWN required-updates system (includes/Updates/NF_Updates_Cache*, run via NF_Abstracts_RequiredUpdate on an admin-context hook) executes during `wp duo apply`'s own WP-CLI process boot and writes a premature/partial nf3_upgrades row for the new form AFTER duo's own invalidate call already ran earlier in the SAME process. Rather than ship a guess as fact, this manifest takes the same posture DUO-3272's polylang rebuilder already established for a different plugin's own apply-skipped-hooks gap: a rebuilder that unconditionally REBUILDS (not merely invalidates) every form's nf3_upgrades cache from the FINAL, fully-committed post-apply state, via Ninja Forms' own `WPN_Helper::build_nf_cache()` (the exact function NF's own save path calls to populate this cache normally) -- correct regardless of which exact code path left a stale entry, and a strict superset of what the existing invalidate declaration already does. Never a script-side warm-fetch: that would hide a real defect real operators hit on every apply, not fix it. Pair budget freed up after this was written -- attempted a controlled A/B reproduction on an isolated pair (own site-repo, own capture/apply round-trip, a real 4-field form landing at the SAME id=1 the actual fixture's target lands at after reset_env_state's own truncate, immediate curl fetch matching the fixture's own methodology) both WITH and WITHOUT this rebuilder declared. Neither reproduced the empty-first-render symptom -- both fetches, both configurations, rendered identically and correctly, nf3_upgrades staying genuinely empty throughout. Recorded honestly rather than quietly dropped: this does not mean the rebuilder is unnecessary (the underlying mechanism it targets is real and independently confirmed, per the trace above), only that whatever ADDITIONALLY differs in the actual r1a1/r1a2 fixture -- the real 23-field/3-action form's specific content, some other request-path difference between this isolated pair and the shared stack, or something else not yet identified -- did not carry over to this smaller reproduction. The rebuilder ships on its own merits (unconditionally correct, matches the DUO-3272 precedent, zero cost when Ninja Forms did no work); round 4 against the real fixture is the test that actually confirms or refutes it for the original symptom.

DUO-3338 (structured actions supersede the free-form `rebuilders` channel): the `wp eval` payload that looped Ninja_Forms()->form()->get_forms() calling WPN_Helper::build_nf_cache() is now provider `ninja-forms-form-cache` capability `rebuild_form_caches` (manifests/providers/ninja-forms-form-cache.php), which ports that loop unchanged and stays unscoped exactly as the declaration was. The rebuild-not-merely-invalidate reasoning recorded below, and the per-row `invalidate` declaration it contrasts itself with, are both unchanged; only the channel that carries the rebuild changed, plus a checked readback per rebuilt form so a silent no-op can no longer pass as success.
